meta.title: Furifont: furigana built into the font
meta.description: A Japanese font that shows furigana by itself.

footer.fonts: The fonts use the {license}. They come from Source Han Sans and Source Han Serif.
footer.data: The readings come from {jmdict}, {jmnedict}, {kanjidic} (EDRDG), {furigana}, {japanpost} (place names) and {desktoptetsu} (JR stations). They use the CC BY-SA 4.0 license.
footer.code: The tools use the MIT license.

editable: Sample text. You can edit it.

hero.body: Furifont is a Japanese font that shows furigana on the font itself. With the ligatures to adopt to pronunciation of words. Works everywhere supporting custom fonts.

notice: Furigana might be incorrect due to the limits of fonts, so keep that in mind.

playground.okuriganaHint: This requires JavaScript. Font cannot handle okurigana due to browser's limitations.
playground.textHint: Click the text to edit it.

build.title: Customized build
build.body: Furifont is compiled from a base font, Source Han Sans or Serif. A build step reads a dictionary of thousands of words and draws the furigana into new glyphs. The result is a normal font file. It needs no JavaScript and no plugin.

ligatures.title: Ligatures do the work
ligatures.body: For each word, the font holds a ligature. For example, 今日 becomes one glyph with きょう above it. The swap happens when the text is drawn, so the text itself does not change.

longest.title: Longest word first
longest.body: Furifont compares each group of kanji with a list of thousands of common words. It tries the longest word first. For example, it picks 日本語 before 日本. It reads 今日 as one word, きょう.

bare.title: No furigana when unsure
bare.body: A single kanji gets furigana only when one reading is clearly the most likely. 大人気 can be read だいにんき or おとなげ, so Furifont shows no furigana.

okurigana.title: Opt-in Okurigana
okurigana.body: Browsers shape each font script separately, so the font cannot see the kana after a kanji (which is called okurigana). We provide optional support for it through JavaScript annotation.

selectors.body: Some words have more than one common reading. Furifont shows the most common one. To choose another, put a variation selector (an invisible character) right after the first kanji. VS226 gives reading 1, VS227 gives reading 2, and so on. VS225 removes the furigana.

downloads.formats: OTF and TTF are commonly used for installing on your computer. WOFF2 is optimized for websites. We recommend the variable fonts for the best experience. In some cases you may need the static weights for compatibility.
downloads.buildOwn: Or build your own font. You can choose another base font, a list with fewer or more words, other furigana letters, or other sizes.

anyPage.body: You can use Furifont on any website. Lines with kanji get extra space for the furigana. If Furifont is installed on your computer, nothing downloads. If it is not, the font loads from this site.
anyPage.bookmarkletHint: Drag it to your bookmarks bar. On any page, click it to turn Furifont on. Click it again to turn Furifont off. Some sites, such as X and GitHub, do not let fonts load from other sites. On those sites, install Furifont on your computer.
anyPage.okuriganaHint: Picks the right reading of a kanji before its okurigana, such as 来 in 来る and 来ない.
anyPage.userscriptHint: This works with Tampermonkey or Violentmonkey (browser add-ons that run small scripts). It turns Furifont on by itself on Japanese pages. It also works on sites that do not let fonts load from other sites. Its menu lets you switch to another Furifont font or turn it off.

toast.message: Furifont could not load its font on this page. Some sites, such as X and GitHub, do not let fonts load from other sites. On those sites, you must install Furifont on your computer.
toast.outdated: A newer version of Furifont is out.

reference.title: Pick a reading
reference.body: Furifont shows the most common reading of a word. To show another reading, put a variation selector (an invisible character) right after the first kanji of the word. VS226 gives reading 1, VS227 gives reading 2, and so on. After a single kanji, the selector chooses the reading of that kanji. VS225 shows the kanji with no furigana.
reference.search: Search a word or kanji: 市場, 今日, 生
reference.hint: Click a reading to copy the word with its selector.
reference.unavailable: The reference comes with the ready-made fonts, and it could not load here ({error}). Build the fonts with {command}, or open Customize.

report.title: Report a wrong reading
report.body: Did Furifont show the wrong furigana, or none where a word needs it? Tell us the words and the readings they should have. You can report several words at once. We go through the reports to fix the dictionary.
report.notePlaceholder: Anything that helps, for example the browser, or why the reading is wrong.
report.name: Your name (optional)
report.nameHint: To credit you when the reading is fixed. Leave it empty to stay anonymous.
report.failed: The report could not be sent. Try again later.
report.limited: You sent many reports in a short time. Try again in an hour.
report.privacy: We store what you enter here, the font version and your browser name. We do not store your IP address.

offline.title: Build your own Furifont
offline.body: Customize is a tool that runs on your computer. It reads your base fonts and saves the fonts that it builds. Start it in any folder. Then this page opens with a live preview, the dictionary, and a Build button. The new fonts go in {folder}.
offline.needs: You need Node 22.18 or later (a free program that runs JavaScript tools).

auth.title: Enter the code from your terminal
auth.body: {command} showed a six-digit code in your terminal (the window where you started it).
auth.failed: That code did not work. Check the terminal and try again.

options.baseHint: The font to add furigana to. Use a font to download, such as Source Han Serif JP Bold, or the path to another font file on your computer.
options.skipHint: Of the words left, the most common get no furigana, because a reader already knows them. Words and single kanji are sorted by how common they are, in steps of 500.
options.wordsHint: The next words, the most common first. In all, {count} words get furigana.
options.jlptHint: Words on the JLPT lists (for the Japanese-Language Proficiency Test) up to this level get no furigana. N5 is the easiest level.

jmdict.name: All JMdict words
jmdict.hint: JMdict: every word, including those no list ranks, such as 四字熟語. Those fill the text nothing else matches, and add about 700 KB to the font.

ichi.name: Basic words
ichi.hint: JMdict "ichi1" and "ichi2": words from the Ichimango list (a list of basic words).

news.name: Newspaper words
news.hint: JMdict "news1" and "news2": the 24,000 words that appear most often in newspapers.

spec.name: Everyday words
spec.hint: JMdict "spec1" and "spec2": common words that the other lists miss, such as 日本.

gai.name: Loanwords
gai.hint: JMdict "gai1" and "gai2": common words that Japanese borrowed from other languages.

nf.name: Newspaper ranking
nf.hint: JMdict "nf01" to "nf48": the words the newspaper list ranks, 500 words a step.

tatoeba.name: Tatoeba sentences
tatoeba.hint: Tatoeba: words that its example sentences use three times or more, such as 留守中, even when no list above has them.

place.name: Place names
place.hint: JMnedict: stations and places. Furifont uses them where no common word matches the text.

mahjong-yaku.name: Mahjong yaku
mahjong-yaku.hint: Names of the scoring hands and tiles of mahjong, such as 立直. Furifont uses them where no common word matches the text.

jr-stations.name: JR stations
jr-stations.hint: Names of JR stations, such as 阿蘇, from the Desktop Tetsu list. Furifont uses them where no common word matches the text.

yojijukugo.name: Four-character idioms
yojijukugo.hint: JMdict: yojijukugo, such as 阿鼻叫喚. Furifont uses them where no common word matches the text.

japan-post.name: Municipalities and towns
japan-post.hint: Names of municipalities and towns, such as 一宮, from Japan Post's postal code data. Furifont uses them where no common word matches the text.

options.shareHint: A single kanji gets furigana only when one reading makes up at least this share of its uses in the dictionary. Use a number from 0.5 to 1. A higher number gives furigana to fewer kanji.
options.resetHint: Go back to the settings that Customize loaded. Your words stay.

overview.hint: Words sampled at an even distance from each part of the dictionary, most common first.

dictionary.search: Search the dictionary: 今日, 生
dictionary.hint: These words have several common readings. Pin one to make it the default reading.
